AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why should broken glass be kept out of compost? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the heap too wet
   B. It rots too fast
   C. It smells bad
   D. It does not rot and can cut people

2. Which of these is a brown material for a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Vegetable peelings
   B. Fresh cow dung
   C. Fresh weeds
   D. Dry leaves

3. Why should the end of the drip pipe be closed? (1 mark)
   A. So the pipe looks nice
   B. So water does not run out of the end
   C. So the plants do not drink
   D. So rainwater cannot enter

4. How far from the plant should the bottle drip be placed? (1 mark)
   A. About 10 to 15 cm
   B. Two metres
   C. Exactly on top of the stem
   D. In the next field

5. Why is dry firewood better than wet firewood? (1 mark)
   A. It cannot burn
   B. It puts out fires
   C. It burns better with less smoke
   D. It is heavier

6. What is used to make the arms of a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. A shorter stick tied across the pole
   B. Sand
   C. A bottle
   D. A bucket of water

7. How do bees and butterflies help crops and fruit trees? (1 mark)
   A. They water the plants
   B. They eat the fruit
   C. They carry pollen from flower to flower
   D. They dig the soil

8. Which is the best material for stuffing a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. Dry grass
   B. Glass
   C. Wet mud
   D. Stones

9. What word means living peacefully together with wild animals? (1 mark)
   A. Hunting
   B. Coexisting
   C. Trapping
   D. Poaching

10. How deep should tiny seeds be sown? (1 mark)
   A. About 30 cm
   B. About 1 cm
   C. As deep as a hand
   D. On top of a heap

11. When should the grass mulch be removed? (1 mark)
   A. At sowing
   B. After harvesting
   C. When seedlings begin to appear
   D. Never

12. What is a seedling? (1 mark)
   A. A ripe fruit
   B. A young plant grown from a seed
   C. A dry stick
   D. A type of soil

13. What can an agricultural extension officer help with? (1 mark)
   A. Building a house
   B. Cooking meals
   C. Selling your tools
   D. Advice on which varieties and methods suit your area

14. What is pruning? (1 mark)
   A. Harvesting fruit
   B. Watering the plant
   C. Planting a seed
   D. Cutting off dead, weak or unwanted branches

15. Which of these is a sign of a healthy young fruit plant? (1 mark)
   A. Green leaves and steady growth
   B. Rotten stem
   C. Yellow and dry leaves
   D. Fallen stem

16. Which nutrient do oranges and guavas supply in large amounts? (1 mark)
   A. Starch
   B. Salt
   C. Cooking oil
   D. Vitamin C

17. Which of these is an animal welfare need? (1 mark)
   A. Clean water always available
   B. Being hit
   C. No shelter
   D. Living in mud

18. Why should raw milk be boiled before drinking? (1 mark)
   A. To make it blue
   B. To make it thicker
   C. To make it colder
   D. To kill germs

19. Which of these is a protective food? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking oil
   B. Sukuma wiki
   C. Ugali
   D. Sugar

20. Which food is a good source of protein and cheap in many homes? (1 mark)
   A. Salt
   B. Soda
   C. Sugar
   D. Beans

21. Which of these is used for shallow frying? (1 mark)
   A. A cup
   B. A bowl
   C. A frying pan
   D. A bucket

22. Why should vegetables be boiled for a short time only? (1 mark)
   A. It saves nothing
   B. Long boiling makes them colder
   C. Long boiling destroys some vitamins
   D. Short boiling makes them poisonous

23. Why is it a good idea to use the water from boiled vegetables in soup? (1 mark)
   A. It is dirty
   B. It has no use
   C. It contains vitamins that came out of the vegetables
   D. It is poisonous

24. What should you do if oil in a pan catches fire? (1 mark)
   A. Pour water on it
   B. An adult covers the pan with a lid and turns off the heat
   C. Blow on it
   D. Carry the pan outside quickly

25. How can you make drinking water safe? (1 mark)
   A. Leave it in the sun uncovered
   B. Stir it with a stick
   C. Boil it and let it cool covered
   D. Add soil

26. What is the correct order for cleaning a room? (1 mark)
   A. Sweep, mop, dust
   B. Dust, sweep, mop
   C. Mop, sweep, dust
   D. Mop, dust, sweep

27. What do you use to scrub gumboots? (1 mark)
   A. A hammer
   B. A knife
   C. A heavy stone
   D. A soft brush with soapy water

28. Which PPE protects the head from sun and dust? (1 mark)
   A. Gumboots
   B. Dust mask
   C. Gloves
   D. Headgear

29. What is a pin cushion used for? (1 mark)
   A. Cutting cloth
   B. Ironing cloth
   C. Measuring cloth
   D. Keeping needles and pins safe

30. Which tool holds a needle safely on the finger to push it? (1 mark)
   A. Ruler
   B. Scissors
   C. Thimble
   D. Pin cushion

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. State three safety rules when using needles and scissors. (3 marks)

32. Give three uses of goats. (3 marks)

33. Name three foods that can be shallow fried. (3 marks)

34. Give three benefits of using compost manure on the farm. (3 marks)

35. Sila has a millet field where birds eat the grain every morning. Suggest and explain a plan to protect the crop without killing the birds. (5 marks)

36. Explain the difference between domestic and wild animals. (2 marks)

37. Prepare a balanced menu for one day for a Grade 4 child using local foods and explain why it is balanced. (5 marks)

38. Name three crops established by direct sowing of tiny seeds. (3 marks)

39. Describe how to shallow fry an egg. (4 marks)

40. What is personal protective equipment (PPE)? (2 marks)

41. Explain the difference between green and brown materials for compost, with an example of each. (3 marks)

42. Name three methods of cleaning the home environment. (3 marks)

43. Give two advantages of boiling food. (2 marks)

44. Plan a class display of cleaned PPE. Say what you would show and what information cards you would write. (5 marks)

45. Why should tiny seeds be sown shallowly? (2 marks)

46. Explain why we must not leave a fire burning after cooking. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — It does not rot and can cut people
   Glass never rots and can injure anyone handling the compost.

2. D — Dry leaves
   Brown materials are dry, like dry leaves, dry grass and straw.

3. B — So water does not run out of the end
   An open end would waste water.

4. A — About 10 to 15 cm
   Close enough for the roots to reach the water.

5. C — It burns better with less smoke
   Dry wood gives more heat and less smoke.

6. A — A shorter stick tied across the pole
   The cross stick forms shoulders and arms.

7. C — They carry pollen from flower to flower
   Pollination helps fruits and seeds to form.

8. A — Dry grass
   Dry grass is light and easy to use.

9. B — Coexisting
   To coexist is to live together.

10. B — About 1 cm
   The smaller the seed, the shallower it should be sown.

11. C — When seedlings begin to appear
   Seedlings need light.

12. B — A young plant grown from a seed
   A seedling is a young plant.

13. D — Advice on which varieties and methods suit your area
   Extension officers advise farmers.

14. D — Cutting off dead, weak or unwanted branches
   Pruning helps light and air reach the plant.

15. A — Green leaves and steady growth
   Healthy plants grow green.

16. D — Vitamin C
   Citrus fruits and guavas are rich in vitamin C.

17. A — Clean water always available
   Animals need water, feed, shelter, health care and kind treatment.

18. D — To kill germs
   Boiling makes it safe.

19. B — Sukuma wiki
   Vegetables give vitamins and minerals.

20. D — Beans
   Beans are protein-rich.

21. C — A frying pan
   A flat pan holds a little oil.

22. C — Long boiling destroys some vitamins
   Vitamins are lost with too much cooking.

23. C — It contains vitamins that came out of the vegetables
   Some vitamins go into the cooking water.

24. B — An adult covers the pan with a lid and turns off the heat
   Water makes an oil fire worse.

25. C — Boil it and let it cool covered
   Boiling kills germs.

26. B — Dust, sweep, mop
   Dust falls, so dust before sweeping.

27. D — A soft brush with soapy water
   A soft brush avoids damage.

28. D — Headgear
   Hats, caps and scarves cover the head.

29. D — Keeping needles and pins safe
   It holds sharp objects.

30. C — Thimble
   A thimble protects the finger.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Never put needles in the mouth; keep them in a pin cushion; count them; carry scissors with points down (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: Meat, milk, skins, manure and income (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: Eggs, fish, sausages, onions, chapati (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: It feeds crops, it softens the soil and helps it to hold water, and it is cheap because it uses waste.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct benefit.

35. (5 marks)
   Answer: Make a scarecrow with tins and shiny strips, place it in the field, move it every few days, and use a net or a noise maker. Avoid poison because it harms other living things.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for scarecrow and moving it, 1 mark for another method, 1 mark for avoiding poison, 1 mark for reason.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: Domestic animals are kept and cared for by people. Wild animals live freely in nature.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.

37. (5 marks)
   Answer: Breakfast: porridge and egg; lunch: ugali, beans and sukuma wiki; supper: rice, fish and cabbage with fruit. It includes energy, body-building and protective foods in every day.
   Working / marking points: 3 marks for a menu with all groups, 2 marks for correct explanation.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Carrot, millet, amaranth, radish, sorghum (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each crop.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Crack the egg into a bowl; heat a little oil in the pan; slide the egg in; cook until the white is firm; lift out with a spatula.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

40. (2 marks)
   Answer: Clothing and gear worn to protect the body from dirt, injury, dust and germs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for clothing or gear, 1 mark for protection.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Green materials are fresh and wet such as fresh grass or peelings. Brown materials are dry such as dry leaves or straw.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for correct examples.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sweeping, dusting, mopping and disposal of refuse (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each method.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: It needs no oil and it makes hard food soft and safe.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each advantage.

44. (5 marks)
   Answer: Display gloves, gumboots, mask, headgear, overall, canvas shoes; cards say what each protects and how to clean it; safe storage; explain to visitors.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for items, 2 marks for cards, 1 mark for explaining.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: They have little stored food so they cannot push up through deep soil.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for little food, 1 mark for not reaching the surface.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: It wastes fuel and can cause a fire or accident.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for waste, 1 mark for danger.
